High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:88365
Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 7412 of 2023
Appellant :- Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Appellant :- Adarsh Kumar,Anil Kumar Rai,Om Prakash Shukla
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Shubhi Singh
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellants with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection
order dated 06.06.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge Sc/St Act, Varanasi in Case Crime
No.149 of 2023, under Sections 147, 419, 420, 467, 468, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)Va
Sc/St Act, 1989, Police Station Badagaon, District Varanasi.

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned AGA and perused the entire record.
3.

The prosecution story as unfolded in the F.I.R. is that the named three accused persons along with four unknown persons procured the forged will deed allegedly executed by Late Ram Naresh,
the father of the informant which was registered on 19.03.2013 and appellant nos.1 & 4 also got mutated their names in the revenue records and when it was produced by the informant, he was Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87869270/
1 threatened for life and were also abused by their caste name.

entities.text: Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
F.I.R. was lodged on 11.05.2023.
4.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that no forgery has been committed by the appellants of this case and they have never made wrongful gain in their favour.
It is next submitted that the alleged incident is said to be happened in the year 2013 and after a long gap of about ten years, the F.I.R. in this matter was lodged.

It is next submitted that in Original Suit No.2912 of 2021 which was filed by the informant, his brother and mother against the appellants nos.1 & 4 and three others in respect of the property in question for cancellation of the will deed and also of the sale deed executed in pursuance of the will deed dated 19.03.2023 which was contested by the defendants.

It is further submitted that on the basis of sale deed, appellant no.1 Irshad Ahmad was recorded in the revenue records but subsequently looking at the mala fide intention of late Ram Naresh, the father of the informant, appellant no.1 filed Original Suit No.511 of 2006 subsequently, a compromise was filed in the said suit and the suit was decided in terms of the compromise.
It was admitted that the defendants who were the legal heirs of the late Ram Naresh have no concern with the land in question.
It is next submitted that in the said suit, an order for interim injunction was passed in favour of Irshad Ahmad, the plaintiff in the said suit.
It is also submitted that despite the interim injunction passed by the competent civil court, an F.I.R. was lodged by the informant in this case concealing the true facts with mala fide intention.

It is next submitted that no prima facie case has been made out against the appellants under Sections 147,
419, 420, 467, 468, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)va SC/ST Act.

It is further submitted that the learned Special court did not consider the evidence and facts on record and the law applicable thereto and the order dated 06.06.2023 rejecting the bail application of the appellants is arbitrary and illegal.
5.

Per contra, learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposing the present appeal and has made a preliminary objection that since Section 18 of the SC/ST Act bars the filing of anticipatory bail application in the matters covered by the SC/ST Act, the application for grant of anticipatory bail moved by the appellants before the Special Judge SC/ST Act, Varanasi was not maintainable in itself and that is why only on this point very ground, the anticipatory bail application was rejected by the said court vide order dated 06.06.2023.
It is next submitted that prima facie, the offence under Section 325A SC/ST Act was made out from the contents of the F.I.R.
It is further submitted that so far as the merit of the case is concerned, the whole story concocted by the appellants is false and frivolous and the appeal as such is liable to be dismissed.
6. On the other hand, learned AGA opposed the present criminal appeal and put forward almost the same contentions as raised by the learned counsel for the informant.

7. Reliance has been placed upon Dashrath Sahu VS. State of Chattisgarh 2024 0 Supreme(SC) 76.
8.

entities.text: Dashrath Sahu VS. State of Chattisgarh 2024 0 Supreme(SC) 76
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case law cited from the appellants side as mentioned above promogates the legal dictum that if the offence is committed with intention that victim belonged to Scheduled Castes category.

The provisions of Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act were also taken into account by Hon'ble the Apex Court and it was held that the offence must be committed upon the present accused belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with intention that it was being done on the ground of caste.

Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87869270/
2

entities.text: Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, in hand, prima facie there is no evidence to this fact that the offence in the present matter was committed upon a person who is a member of SC/ST Community with intention that it was being done on the ground of caste.
9. From the perusal of the record, it appears that the offence in this case was not committed on the ground that the aggrieved party was a member of SC/ST Community.
Hence, the present anticipatory bail application is maintainable.

10. So far as the facts of the case are concerned, there is ample material on record to show that civil suit is pending between the parties in this respect of the property in dispute and earlier a civil suit was also filed between the appellants and father of the informant which resulted into compromise between the parties.
11.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

12. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and particularly, keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the Court is of the opinion that the appellants has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application of the appellants.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.
13. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellants is set-aside.

14. Let the appellants Irshad Ahmad, Faisal Irshad, Arshil Irshad & Ruksana Begum involved in Case Crime No.149 of 2023, under Sections 147, 419, 420, 467, 468, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)Va SC/ST Act, 1989, Police Station Badagaon, District Varanasi be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The appellants will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The appellants will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The appellants will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The appellants shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which they are suspected.

(v) The appellants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87869270/
3 from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

entities.text: Irshad Ahmad Siddiqui And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
